title: Seller Audit & Triage Deck — Quick Ops Draft
body:
Purpose: quick, seller-facing audit + triage deck to (a) diagnose inference integration risk fast, (b) propose immediate pilot guardrails, and (c) surface negotiation levers that keep pilots moving while protecting economics.

Usage notes (seller quick one-pager):
- 3–5 minute prep before demo/account call: open this doc, pick the relevant scenario, run through the kernel questions (Latency / SLO / Data sensitivity).
- If customer asks for an SLA in discovery: use the Triage Ladder to scope pilot instead of promising org-level SLA.
- Keep the pilot ≤ 8 weeks, focus on three measurable outcomes (latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy on sample evals).

Slide 1 — One-line sell: "Keep your app online and predictable without building inference ops"
- Talking points: production-first runtime, fallbacks, dev ergonomics.
- Demo cue: show latency dashboard snippet (mock).

Slide 2 — 90s triage: The Triage Ladder (fast diagnostic)
- Tier A (Latency-sensitive, user-facing sync flows): p95 target <= 250ms; require dedicated capacity or strict routing to low-latency region.
- Tier B (Nearline or async, user-facing embellishments): p95 <= 1.2s; use hosted with KV caching and prefix caching, consider quantized variants.
- Tier C (Batch / offline / embeddings / scoring): throughput-first, use burstable reserved pools, liberal batching.

Quick questions for the ladder (script for seller):
1) Where is the model call in the user flow? (synchronous / async / batch)
2) Acceptable p95 tail for production? (get a number)
3) Rough volume: requests / minute and average tokens per request?
4) Data residency / encryption / compliance must-haves?
5) Can the customer tolerate short degraded output (fallback model) for availability?

Slide 3 — Rapid triage checklist (if customer says "we want production")
- Do they have a sample corpus or test prompts? (Yes -> request 50–200 gold prompts)
- Define 3 success metrics: latency, cost per thousand tokens, user acceptance metric (CTR / retention / accuracy).
- Identify red lines (no cross-tenant logging, no external KMS).
- Ask for a rough traffic shape (peak hour multiplier).

Slide 4 — Pilot guardrails (three-tier guardrail template)
- Canary window: 1% traffic or 100 users for 72 hours.
- Auto-fallback: route to cheaper model variant on 5xx or >2x latency SLO violations.
- Cost cap: soft alerts at 60% of commit, hard throttle at 80% unless exec escalation.
- Data controls: retention TTL 7 days, logs scrubbed for PII unless approved.

Slide 5 — Negotiation heuristics (what sellers can offer vs what to push back on)
- Seller offers (fast wins): short pilot duration, limited traffic window, trial-free reserved hours (small), access to telemetry dashboard, weekly sync.
- Pushback lines (protect economics & ops): org-level latency SLA, unlimited reserved commitments without usage baseline, unlimited debug access to customer infra.
- Trade tools: burst windows (scheduled within month), graded commit (start small -> scale to full commit after proof), rollback credits if performance regressions exceed guardrail.

Script snippets (quick):
- When asked for SLA: "We prefer to scope an 6-week pilot with measurable p95 targets and automatic fallback – once those are met we can discuss formal SLA language tied to committed capacity."
- When pushed on price: "We can give a small reserved bucket for the pilot and a clear overage rate; if you hit X sustained qps we'll help build a scale plan that reduces unit cost."

Slide 6 — Technical red flags to escalate to SE or SRE immediately
- No test prompts or synthetic load available.
- Customer expects synchronous p95 < 200ms at >50 qps on a single model variant (likely needs Dedicated).
- Non-negotiable data residency requiring on-prem deployment now.
- Expectation of unlimited debug access to runtime (we require scoped access).

Slide 7 — Quick ROI sketch (seller-facing math)
- Inputs we ask for: average API calls/day, avg tokens per call, price per 1k tokens baseline, current infra/person-hours spent managing models.
- Example: 50k calls/day x 300 tokens = 15M tokens/day -> at $0.0025/1k = $37.50/day -> show cost delta vs self-host and ops savings.
- Show impact of batching/caching: 30% token reduction -> direct dollar savings.

Slide 8 — Two pilot templates (copyable into SOW)
- Template A: "Latency-first pilot" (4–6 weeks)
  - Deliverables: p95 <= target, telemetry access, canary run, go/no-go review.
  - Redwood commitments: 200 reserved hours, weekly tune, fallback policy.
- Template B: "Cost-down pilot" (6–8 weeks)
  - Deliverables: cost per 1k tokens < target, recommended quantization plan, model variant tests.
  - Redwood commitments: model/quantization consult, cost simulation, 2-week optimization sprint.

Slide 9 — Role play snippets for SEs and sellers
- Objection: "We can't share prompts." -> Reply: "Start with anonymized samples or a small synthetic corpus; without them we can only validate infra not quality."
- Objection: "We need SLA day 1." -> Reply: "We can commit to pilot guardrails and an SLA tied to a committed Dedicated contract after the pilot metrics are met."

Slide 10 — Post-pilot pathing (decision tree)
- Success: scale reserved capacity -> negotiate multi-month commit with volume discounts and extended retention.
- Mixed: limited rollout + targeted mitigations (caching, model tweaks) -> additional optimization sprint.
- Fail: fallback + enablement -> capture learnings, offer extended pilot with MPS (managed performance sprint).

Notes to self / seller tips (rough, shorthand):
- Always ask for "one success metric" early — it keeps pilot scope focused.
- Use the ROI sketch live with customers; change numbers to their inputs.
- Keep fallback story simple: cheaper model or lower-concurrency lane.
- Document every pilot as a case study template (internal page) so next seller can reuse guardrails.

Attachments & next steps (checklist for owner):
- Request: sample prompts + traffic profile + compliance checklist (send template).
- Setup: enable telemetry view + create pilot channel in Slack + schedule kickoff call.
- Internal: create SE ticket with expected infra needs and mark as pilot-urgent.

Open questions we still need to resolve (for product/ops):
- Default cost cap for pilot free reserved hours (what's the org ceiling we can authorize?).
- Standard wording for fallback credits and rollback SLA language.
- Template telemetry dashboard to hand to customers (copyable).


End of doc — quick checklist for call:
- Ask Triage Ladder Qs (flow, p95, volume, compliance).
- Pick Pilot Template (Latency-first or Cost-down).
- Commit to 1 sample metric, request prompts, schedule kickoff.

(Internal tags: prioritize as mid-market seller enablement asset; convert to 6-slide mini-deck + 1-page cheat-sheet.)
